title: Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
summary: Measuring similarity between incomplete data is challenging because traditional methods either discard incomplete samples or impute missing values, causing information loss and bias. This paper proposes the proximity kernel, which projects data into a high-dimensional sparse representation via data-dependent binning and proximity assignment, and handles missing values through a cascading fallback strategy using kernel mean embedding. Experiments on 12 real-world datasets show that the proximity kernel achieves superior clustering performance (NMI) compared to 9 baseline methods while maintaining linear time complexity.

requirements.stmt: Equal-frequency binning per feature using observed values only to select nbins bin centers
Proximity assignment: assign each observed value to its nearest bin center
requirements.quote: Given the bin centers {cj,1, ...,cj,nbins} for each feature j, we assign each observed value to its nearest center.

requirements.stmt: One-hot encoding construction for each feature after bin assignment
requirements.quote: For sample iand each feature j, we construct a binary vector hi,j∈{0, 1}nbins

requirements.stmt: Cascading fallback strategy Level 1: intersection-based exact matching across all observed features
requirements.quote: The first level seeks samples that match sample ion all observed features.

requirements.stmt: Cascading fallback strategy Level 2: union-based partial matching on any observed feature
requirements.quote: we relax the constraint to consider samples that match on any observed feature.

requirements.stmt: Cascading fallback strategy Level 3: global prior distribution when no similar samples found
requirements.quote: we cannot leverage local similarity and must use the global distribution of each missing feature.
